holidays.name: Make Up Your Mind Day
holidays.description: This is the last day of the year to settle all those dilemmas you've been putting off. Pick a New Year's resolution, choose a restaurant, or finally decide what to do about that half-finished project. Anything you can decide today won't follow you into next year.
holidays.origin: This is an unofficial observance of unclear origin. It fits the final day of the year, when people tend to take stock and tie up loose ends.
holidays.funFact: Many people never keep their resolutions, so deciding on one today may be the easy part.

holidays.name: National Champagne Day
holidays.description: Pop the cork. Today is for raising a glass of bubbly to send the old year off in style. It lands on the biggest toasting night of the year.
holidays.origin: This is an unofficial observance of unclear origin. It pairs naturally with New Year's Eve, when sparkling wine is the traditional drink for a midnight toast.
holidays.funFact: True Champagne can only come from the Champagne region of France. Everything else sparkling is technically just sparkling wine.

holidays.name: Hogmanay
holidays.description: This is Scotland's rowdy, days-long New Year's celebration. It includes street parties, fireworks, and singing "Auld Lang Syne" with crossed arms. Tradition also calls for "first-footing." The first person to cross your threshold after midnight should bring gifts such as coal, shortbread, or whisky, and a tall dark-haired visitor is considered the luckiest.
holidays.origin: Hogmanay has roots in Norse winter solstice festivities and older Scottish customs. It became the main midwinter celebration in Scotland for centuries, partly because Christmas was downplayed there after the Reformation.
holidays.funFact: Edinburgh hosts one of the world's biggest Hogmanay street parties. Some Scots also swing fireballs through the streets in Stonehaven.
